args.region: porta hepatis and portal vein region in the central liver/upper abdomen
porta hepatis and portal vein region in the central liver/upper abdomen

output.text:
**Image type:** Axial contrast-enhanced CT of the upper abdomen.

**Region evaluated:** Porta hepatis / portal vein region in the central liver-upper abdomen. This region can be localized on this image, though detail is limited by image resolution.

**Relevant radiologic features:**
- **Portal vein/porta hepatis appearance:** A contrast-opacified vascular structure is visible in the porta hepatis region, consistent with the portal vein.
- **Density:** The vessel appears relatively high attenuation/enhancing compared with adjacent liver parenchyma. No definite intraluminal low-density filling defect is confidently seen on this single image.
- **Margins/shape:** The visible portal venous structure has smooth, rounded/tubular margins without obvious abrupt contour irregularity.
- **Size:** No gross portal vein enlargement is evident on this image.
- **Adjacent porta hepatis:** No clearly defined mass or bulky lymphadenopathy is identifiable in the porta hepatis region on this limited view.

**Impression:** On this single axial CT image, the porta hepatis/portal vein region shows an enhancing portal venous structure without a definite visible filling defect, mass, or gross abnormal enlargement. Assessment is limited by the single low-resolution image.

localization.requested: porta hepatis and portal vein region in the central liver/upper abdomen

hepatic veins and inferior vena cava near the liver

output.text:
**Image type:** Axial contrast-enhanced CT image of the upper abdomen.

**Region of interest:** Hepatic veins and inferior vena cava (IVC) near the liver.

**Findings relevant to CT/radiology:**
- The **IVC** is identifiable posterior/central near the liver, anterior to the vertebral body. It appears **rounded to oval**, with **smooth margins** and **contrast attenuation** consistent with an opacified venous structure.
- No definite **intraluminal filling defect**, abrupt narrowing, or external compression is visible in the IVC on this single image.
- The **hepatic veins** near their drainage into the IVC are only **partially/poorly visualized** due to image resolution and single-slice limitation. I cannot confidently assess all hepatic vein branches.
- No obvious mass or abnormal density is seen directly involving the visible hepatic venous/IVC region on this image.

**Limitations:** Assessment is limited by the single low-resolution axial image; full evaluation of hepatic veins/IVC would require the complete contrast-enhanced CT series.

args.region: splenic vein, superior mesenteric vein, and portal-splenic confluence
splenic vein, superior mesenteric vein, and portal-splenic confluence

output.text:
**Image type:** Axial contrast-enhanced abdominal CT image.

**Region of interest:** Splenic vein, superior mesenteric vein (SMV), and portal-splenic confluence.

**Localization confidence:** The portal-splenic confluence region can be approximately localized centrally, anterior to the aorta and near the pancreatic region. However, the full course of the splenic vein and SMV is not confidently traceable on this single low-resolution axial image.

**Relevant radiology features in the visible ROI:**
- **Density/enhancement:** The visible central venous structures appear contrast-opacified. No definite low-density intraluminal filling defect is identifiable on this image.
- **Shape/caliber:** No obvious focal venous expansion or marked narrowing is apparent in the visible confluence region.
- **Margins:** The visible vessel margins are not sharply resolved due to image quality, but no gross irregular mass-like vascular contour is evident.
- **Size:** Accurate measurement is not possible from this image alone; no obvious gross enlargement is seen.

**Impression:** Within the limitations of a single low-resolution CT slice, there is **no definite visible thrombus or occlusion** at the portal-splenic confluence/SMV region. Full assessment of the splenic vein and SMV would require the complete contrast-enhanced CT series.

args.region: any visible abdominal venous structures with intraluminal filling defect or thrombosis
any visible abdominal venous structures with intraluminal filling defect or thrombosis

output.text:
**Image type:** Axial contrast-enhanced abdominal CT.

**Region of interest:** Visible abdominal venous structures at the porta hepatis/central upper abdomen.

**Findings relevant to radiology:**
- There is a **low-attenuation intraluminal filling defect** within an enhancing venous structure at the **porta hepatis**, most consistent with involvement of the **main portal vein/portal venous confluence region**.
- The defect appears **central to eccentric** within the contrast-opacified lumen.
- Margins are relatively **well defined** by surrounding enhancing blood.
- Exact size cannot be confidently measured from this single low-resolution image, but it appears to involve a **short segment** of the vessel.
- No confident assessment of extension into more distal portal branches, splenic vein, or superior mesenteric vein can be made on this single image.

**Impression:** Findings are suspicious for **portal venous intraluminal thrombus/filling defect**, likely involving the main portal vein region.

localization.requested: any visible abdominal venous structures with intraluminal filling defect or thrombosis
